name: Teikametrics
summary: Advertising optimisation for Amazon and Walmart sellers, with inventory and catalogue signals.
best_for: Amazon and Walmart sellers spending enough on ads that a few points of efficiency covers the fee — under $10K a month the flat $149 is straightforward
skip_if: your ad spend is small or seasonal, because the flat fee at low spend is a large share of your budget and the percentage model at high spend needs modelling before you commit
honest_knock:
Read the Advanced tier carefully, because it is not a subscription — it is a subscription plus a percentage. Three per cent of ad spend above $10,000 means a seller spending $40,000 a month pays an extra $900 on top of whatever the custom base is, and that line scales with the thing the product is supposed to make more efficient. That is not automatically wrong — it aligns them with your growth — but it does mean your bill rises when your advertising does, and you should model it at your expected spend rather than your current one. The $10K threshold is the number to watch: crossing it changes the pricing model, not just the price.

The 3% does not stop when the subscription does. The billing article says that even after cancellation you still incur the 3% monthly charge on any ad spend over $10K unless your connected merchants are removed, and that removal is done by contacting support; the same applies on the free Basic plan you are moved to when you cancel. A seller who cancels at $30,000 a month of ad spend and forgets the merchant connection keeps paying $600 a month for a plan it no longer uses.

The two official price lists disagree above $10K. The pricing page shows Advanced as custom pricing plus 3%; the help article prices Advanced at $1,199 to $1,439 a month without mentioning the 3%, and adds an Essentials Tier 2 at $499 to $599 plus 3% that the pricing page does not list. Get the tier name, the base fee and the percentage in writing before you connect an account that spends more than $10K.

The contract terms are written for a fixed term. Orders renew automatically for the same length unless you give written notice (email is enough) at least 15 days before the term ends; the customer has no right to terminate for convenience, and ending early means paying the fees for the rest of the term within 30 days. Late invoices can carry 1.5% interest a month, and disputes go to the courts of Massachusetts. Only Essentials can be cancelled on the billing page; on Advanced or Enterprise you cancel through your Customer Success Manager or product support.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Essentials, up to $10K a month in ad spend · per month billed annually
pricing.notes: (2026-08-30, re-read on their own pricing page from a US exit; unchanged on 2026-10-13) Essentials, for up to $10K a month in ad spend: $149 a month billed annually, or $179 billed monthly. Advanced, for over $10K a month in ad spend: custom pricing plus 3% of ad spend above $10K. Enterprise, for over $100K a month in ad spend: also custom pricing plus 3% of ad spend above $10K. A free trial and a free opportunity assessment are offered. Re-read on 28 October 2026 with a plain fetch: teikametrics.com/pricing is unchanged (Essentials $149 a month on the annual plan or $179 monthly up to $10K of monthly ad spend; Advanced and Enterprise 'Custom Pricing' with '+3% of ad spend over $10K'). Teikametrics' own help article 'Billing, Plans and Pricing Information' (dated 25 September 2025, read 28 October 2026) still publishes a fully priced ladder that the pricing page does not show: a free Basic plan without the AI features; Essentials Tier 1 ($0 to $10K of monthly ad spend) at $179 monthly or $149 a month with 12 months billed upfront; Essentials Tier 2 ($10K and up) at $599 monthly or $499 a month billed upfront, plus 3% of monthly ad spend over $10K; Advanced at $1,439 monthly or $1,199 a month billed upfront; and Enterprise on custom pricing. The article says the tier is set by your previous 30 days of ad spend, that paying a year upfront saves 20%, and that unused time on a yearly plan is not refunded.
